rules: Pick the first task, in file order, whose status is todo and whose depends_on tasks all pass.
Skip tasks with human set to true unless the owner is taking part; set them to blocked and state in evidence what the owner must decide or check.
Set status to in_progress and owner to your agent name before starting.
Change only status, owner, passes, and evidence fields.
One task is one pull request, and the pull request marks the task done in this file.
Set passes to true only after every acceptance item is verified.
Put the verification command output summary in evidence.
Never edit, remove, or weaken acceptance items without the owner's approval.
Write the failing tests for a task's acceptance items before implementing, and never edit those tests while implementing (the Product Owner flow, T1-12).

A playback task is one whose change makes the app send a media, playlist, segment, subtitle, trickplay or artwork request, or a playstate report. It passes only when its wire test passes against Jellyscale: the Authorization header on every request, no token in any URL, no redirect followed, no other origin contacted.

A task whose title names a Jellyscale issue waits for that issue: set it to blocked with the issue's state in evidence. Nothing may depend on such a task, and the release does not wait for it. Never work around a missing server feature with a token in a URL.
Set status to blocked and explain in evidence when a dependency, an owner decision, or a Shield check is missing.
Use the model and skill named on the task.
Tasks with human set to true need the owner: a decision on look, wording or direction, or a check on the Nvidia Shield. The acceptance names it.
The Product Owner (Fable 5.2) owns the backlog and the priorities: only a Product Owner pass adds, splits, reorders or drops tasks, after triaging tasks/backlog.jsonl. The owner can veto any of it.
Append deferred or newly found work to the backlog (tasks/backlog.jsonl once T1-10 lands); any agent or pull request may.

Before adopting any dependency, verify from primary sources that it is actively maintained: recent releases and commits, not archived, and no maintainer statement of maintenance mode or supersession. Record the check in the task's spec, and re-check every dependency when a phase starts.
There is no done.json. The desktop app's task list lives only in the tag desktop-tauri-final.
Never commit a server address, a credential, or the owner's name.
Read tasks through `pnpm task` (next, show, list, set); never load tasks/prd.json whole. Keep evidence to 600 characters naming the PR or commit.

acceptance: The page opens with focus on Resume S1 E2 or Play S1 E3, naming the episode that will play

No URL, id, path or token is shown

phases.name: Player
phases.goal: Play the original file through Media3 with the header on every request, fall back to an honest conversion, and get subtitles, tracks, skip and Up Next right.
exit: Every sample the device can decode direct plays on the emulator and the Shield, with no server job
A converted session plays over HLS through the validating parser, and the player says so with the reason
Subtitles are drawn on the device and tracks follow the server's defaults
Skip intro, skip credits and Up Next work with the select key alone
Every playback task's wire test passes against Jellyscale

tasks.title: Build the player module's typed seam
acceptance: modules/player is a local Expo module whose methods are exactly the PlayerEngine port's: initialize, launch, pause, seek, select track, stop; a test fails when one is added without updating the allowlist and docs/security.md
A launch takes the typed request union and refuses any other shape; it takes no header, token or free-form option
The module gets its authority to send the header from native code as decision 0005 says, never from an argument
Events map one to one to the core's player events, and errors are codes with no URL, path or player text
A native view hosts the video; React passes it no URL
Kotlin sits behind an interface that a Swift implementation can mirror later; nothing in the TypeScript side names Media3
The play-session id and item ids appear in no log or event payload beyond what the port defines

tasks.title: Direct-play the original file with Media3
acceptance: An original-file launch plays through an ExoPlayer built only with Octave's media source factory over the one OkHttp client, on a SurfaceView
The first-frame event fires when a frame is presented, not when loading starts
The engine reports the decoder's name and whether it is a hardware decoder from what Media3 reports, and unknown when it cannot tell
Seeking, pausing and stopping work, and stop releases the player and the surface
A redirect on the media request ends in a typed error and the other origin receives nothing
The H.264, HEVC and AV1 samples reach first frame on the CI emulator where it has a decoder, and a sample with no decoder ends in the typed cannot-play code
Jellyscale wire test: a capture of a play from the pinned Jellyscale shows the header on every request, range requests included, no credential parameter, and only original-file URLs
tasks.verify: pnpm check && pnpm tv:native:test && pnpm tv:wire

tasks.title: Run a viewing through the coordinator and report playstate
acceptance: Pressing Play negotiates through the core, launches the module and shows the player screen; no other code builds a media URL
The start report is sent after the first frame, progress every 10 s and on pause and seek, and stopped on Back, end and error
An error stop is reported as failed, so the server records no progress for it
Resuming on another client lands within 10 s of where this one stopped
A failed report shows Couldn't save your progress once and never stops playback
Back during loading cancels the attempt and sends no report
From Home, one press on Resume reaches the first frame at the saved position, and returning to Home shows the new position on the card without a restart

The screen stays awake while playing and may sleep while paused for the system's timeout

tasks.title: Hold to scrub with the remote
acceptance: Holding Left or Right for half a second pauses the picture and moves a pending position in growing steps, never more than a fiftieth of the duration per step
The select key commits the pending position; Back returns to where playback was

tasks.title: Show what is really playing in the info sheet
acceptance: An Info control opens a side sheet with Playback, Video, Audio and Decoder sections while the video keeps playing

tasks.title: Report what this device can decode and convert what it cannot
acceptance: The module reports the device's capabilities from the platform's codec list: per codec and profile whether a hardware decoder exists, the HDR types the display supports, and passthrough formats

tasks.title: Play converted streams over HLS through a validating parser
acceptance: An HLS launch is accepted only for a master URL that passes every vector in tests/fixtures/hls-master-urls.json's rules, checked again in Kotlin

Media3 reads playlists only through Octave's parser hook, which refuses the whole playlist unless every URI line and URI attribute is HTTP or HTTPS on the server's origin with no user info, fragment or credential parameter
The Kotlin validator gives the expected verdict for every vector in tests/fixtures/hls-playlists.json, in a JVM test that CI requires
A playlist that names a credential parameter or contains the token value fails the launch closed, and the token appears in no error, event or log

A cross-origin variant, segment, map or key URI ends in the unsafe-stream refusal and the other origin receives nothing
Playlists and segments are fetched only through the one OkHttp client; a segment redirect is not followed

Jellyscale wire test: a server-initiated converted session (the forced-limit sample) from the pinned Jellyscale shows the header on the master, variant, init and segment requests and no credential parameter on any
tasks.verify: pnpm check && pnpm tv:native:test && pnpm tv:wire
